items.excerpt: Democratic Republic of the Congo As the deadly Ebola disease outbreak reached an eighth province of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), investigators pursued all leads on Thursday to assess the risk of the disease spreading in Nigeria. Authorities in Abuja confirmed their first case of infection in an individual arriving from Uganda, which borders the worst-hit provinces in DRC. “The source of exposure is still not known and the travel history of the patient is being pieced together now in terms of her movement from Uganda up to Nigeria,” said Dr Patrick Otim, from the UN World Health Organization (WHO)’s Emergency Response programme, in an online update. “This is rapidly evolving. As we get more information, we’ll try to determine where she was exposed. And then it’s at that point where we can say whether there is any transmission happening”. Nigeria is the fifth country this year after DRC, France, Uganda and Kenya to confirm the presence of Ebola disease caused by Bundibugyo virus. The original DRC outbreak was declared in mid-May where it has led to more than 4,600 deaths and a total of 9,552 confirmed infections. Around six in 10 of these deaths have occurred outside health centres, indicating the continuing difficulty of halting community transmission. The latest DRC province to confirm infections is Nord Ubangi, which borders Central African Republic, where ongoing armed violence continues to uproot thousands of people, increasing the difficulty of halting transmission. – UN News DR Congo: Ebola responders under pressure as outbreak expands ... items.title: Gold heads for steep weekly loss as oil prices fuel Fed rate concerns
items.excerpt: Speculators are trying to defend the key $4,000 level for gold because a clean break below would signal that the market has stopped pricing rate relief and started pricing sticky inflation, elevated yields, and a stronger dollar, said Monte Safieddine, head of market research at Capital.com. Oil prices rose about 4% to a five-month high on Thursday after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked concerns of further disruption to energy supplies. Elevated energy prices bolster expectations of higher-for-longer interest rates by the Fed, increasing the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion. "Any further escalation on the geopolitical front risks pushing oil even higher. Higher oil is reviving inflation fears, lifting yields, and delaying Fed easing. That is a difficult cocktail for bullion," Safieddine added. Focus has turned to the Fed's October 27-28 policy meeting and next week's Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) data, a closely watched gauge as it is the central bank's preferred inflation measure as it targets a 2% inflation rate. Traders are largely expecting the central bank to leave interest rates unchanged next week, but expectations for an interest rate hike in December remain at 80%.

items.title: Oil prices climb above $113 as AI sell-off rattles stocks and investors buy bonds | Euronews
items.excerpt: ## Rising energy prices added to inflation concerns as doubts over AI spending hit tech stocks; investors sought safety in US bonds, and France’s borrowing costs remained above 5%. Asian shares were mostly lower on Friday after the latest sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks weighed on markets around the world, giving the benchmark S&P 500 its worst day since July. Oil prices were hovering at their highest levels since May on worries about the war with Iran, with Brent crude trading at $113.73 per barrel early Friday, up 0.5% after a 4% jump in the previous session. Brent settled at $113.17 on Thursday. US benchmark West Texas Intermediate crude rose 0.6% to $100.08 per barrel. Oil rallied on Thursday as deadly attacks in Saudi Arabia fuelled concerns that a full-scale regional conflict could further choke off global energy supplies. On top of the risk premium, soaring shipping costs are adding to the cost of delivering oil. By mid-October, the cost of shipping crude from the Middle East Gulf to Asia on a large tanker had climbed to over $37 per barrel, more than five times its level before the war began, according to MarketWatch. ... On Thursday, in the US, the S&P 500 fell 1.2%, while the Nasdaq composite tumbled 2.6%. The weakness in tech stocks was so overwhelming that it masked strength elsewhere in the US market, where the majority of stocks actually rose. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added less than 0.1%. AI-related stocks have been swinging on worries that their boom may be under threat because of how expensive it has become to borrow money to build data centres and buy more AI chips. Investors fear share prices shot too high during a years-long frenzy, even though companies in the industry continue to report growth. ... Debt and inflation fears had helped drive a major global bond sell-off, pushing US Treasury yields to their highest levels in decades. But US yields fell sharply on Thursday as investors bought US government bonds in search of something safer to own as AI stocks tumbled. The yield on the 10-year Treasury tumbled to 4.97% from 5.13% late Wednesday and from more than 5.30% earlier this month. The 16-basis-point daily fall was a sharp move for the benchmark yield. Thursday’s drop in yields came even as another report suggested the US economy may be doing better than economists expected. New applications for unemployment benefits fell by 6,000 to 194,000 last week, their lowest level since July, suggesting layoffs remained low. ... Investors will also watch Friday’s preliminary business activity surveys for the eurozone, the UK and the US for signs of how higher energy prices and borrowing costs are affecting growth.

items.title: Justice Department asks appeals court to intervene in California ballot case
items.excerpt: The Justice Department asked an appeals court Thursday to intervene in its lawsuit seeking to temporarily block California from counting more than 20,000 mail-in ballots from voters the Trump administration says are likely not U.S. citizens. The Justice Department asked the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals to get involved before a lower-court judge ruled in the dispute. Justice Department lawyers said the unusual maneuver was necessary because the judge assigned to the case, U.S. District Judge David Carter, had not made a decision by Thursday afternoon, as the department had requested. ... Carter scheduled a hearing for next week to consider the department’s request for an emergency order to block California from counting mail-in ballots from more than 20,000 voters in the Nov. 3 midterm elections until their citizenship status could be verified. The department said it interpreted Carter’s lack of ruling as a “constructive denial” of its request. ... The case is being closely watched as the Trump administration seeks to exert greater control over the elections next month that will determine control of Congress. The Justice Department is considering bringing litigation against more states as part of its efforts to remove noncitizens from voter rolls ahead of the midterms, a department official previously told NBC News. ... Democratic Party leaders have sued in federal court to block the Trump administration from overriding state authority to administer elections or intimidate state and local election officials.

items.title: Senate control hinges on unwanted nominees
items.excerpt: Senate control hinges on unwanted nominees ... Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) and Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) are living out their midterm nightmares — with nominees they didn't want and former colleagues they no longer control. Why it matters: Together, Schumer and Thune are stuck with five Senate races in which their party establishments thought they had a better chance of winning with someone else. - 🤠 Texas: Thune's efforts to stop Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton from winning the party's Senate nomination failed. Now Republicans are spending more than $329 million to defeat state Rep. James Talarico— and it's still a nail-biter. - 🍑 Georgia: GOP leaders couldn't convince Gov. Brian Kemp to run. The eventual nominee, Rep. Mike Collins, has struggled to keep pace with fundraising juggernaut Sen. Jon Ossoff (D). GOP money is in retreat. - 🦞 Maine: Schumer endorsed Gov. Janet Mills, but Graham Platner's implosion left Democrats with backup Troy Jackson against Sen. Susan Collins. - ⛴️ Michigan: Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens and made a name for himself nationally. But he won by just one point even though primary polls showed him up by double digits. He's now polling within the margin of error against the GOP nominee, former Rep. Mike Rogers. - 🏈 Minnesota: Peggy Flanagan ran as a progressive, said she would not support Schumer as leader and bested establishment-backed Rep. Angie Craig. But Cook Political Report moved her race against former NFL sideline reporter Michele Tafoya toward Republicans even as it shifted other races toward Democrats.

items.title: Venezuelans demand elections in first national protest in nearly two years | US-Venezuela Tensions News | Al Jazeera
items.excerpt: Published On 23 Oct 2026 23 Oct 2026 ... Thousands of Venezuelans have taken to the streets in several cities to demand free elections and other political changes, in the first nationwide opposition protest in nearly two years. US President Donald Trump and acting President Delcy Rodriguez have said there would be elections, but no date has been set for a vote to decide on a successor for Nicolas Maduro, after the former Venezuelan president was captured by US forces in a military raid in January. Opposition leader and Nobel Peace Prize winner Maria Corina Machado, who has been outside the country for nearly a year after living in hiding following a contested 2024 election, has said elections must take place by July 2027. Her Vente Venezuela movement organised the protest, which took place in the capital Caracas and other cities, including Valencia, Maracay, San Cristobal and Maracaibo. ... Talks between a faction of the opposition and the interim government, aimed at remaking the top court and the electoral council ahead of eventual elections, held their latest session this month, but changes could take significant time. The negotiations, backed by the US, do not include Machado’s political movement, though she has said she will not stand in the way of their progress. ... Machado’s proxy Edmundo Gonzalez Urrutia claims to have won the 2024 election according to vote tallies by the opposition. But the government, which never released full counts, backed Maduro, as did the country’s legal and electoral institutions.

items.title: LISA, Miley & Kacey Musgraves Lead Best New Music: Friday Music Guide
items.excerpt: This week, LISA drops her new EP; Miley features two new songs on the Nobody Wants This season three soundtrack; Kacey Musgraves shares a taste of her just-announced Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes; and John Mayer is back with a new single and newly-launched label… plus much more. Check out all of this week’s picks below: LISA, Press Play Led by the hard-hitting pop-rap single “SaWaDiKa,” released in September, LISA is now sharing her very first solo EP. Focus track “Tarantino” packs just as hard a punch, while “Cobra” is an attitude-packed dance-pop song and album closer “Sweat” is a sultry song that leaves its subject with a simple instruction — “don’t stress me out” — and its listener wanting more. Press Play follows the 2025 release of LISA’S debut solo full-length, Alter Ego, and arrives just in time for the Thai singer’s upcoming Vegas residency that kicks off in November. — LYNDSEY HAVENS Miley, “Cold Blooded” For longtime Miley fans, the release of “Cold Blooded” has been a long time coming. Written in the late 2010s ahead of her EP She Is Coming, the track never saw the light of day — until now. A demo version of the ballad, which showcases Miley’s undeniable vocal control and power over simple piano chords, is featured as a bonus track on the season three soundtrack for Nobody Wants This, out today. Its one of two Miley demos that made it on the album, as a stripped-down version of her Endless Summer Vacation track “You” also features on the soundtrack and in an episode. The soundtrack is out on Atlantic, while all 10 episodes of season three are now streaming on Netflix. — L. H. Kacey Musgraves, “Weekend In Texas” Kacey Musgraves is previewing her upcoming project Middle of Nowhere Vol. 2: Tex Mex Tapes (out Jan. 15 on Lost Highway Records) with the release of new music, including “Weekend In Texas.” “I’ve got the hat and the cattle to back it up / Everything will be great in my favorite state of mind,” she sings. Bright horns, an irresistible groove and Musgraves’ dulcet vocal tones blend luxuriously as she sings of longing for a soul-restoring few days of escape in the Lone Star State. This new release feels both classic and invigorating. — JESSICA NICHOLSON ... John Mayer, “Tom and Jerry” ... Yung Miami, Watch Dis! After overcoming underdog status to score of the biggest hip-hop hits of 2026 with her New York Knicks-approved “Spend Dat,” Yung Miami has finally unveiled her long-awaited debut solo studio album, Watch Dis. Featuring a wide range of collaborators, including Travis Scott, Summer Walker, Trina, Quavo and more, the 21-track set finds the City Girls alum grounding a revelatory autobiography in the history and culture of her hometown. — KYLE DENIS ... John Legend, Muse After linking up with Clipse and Pharrell Williams for the Let God Sort Em Out standout “The Birds Don’t Sing,” John Legend linked up with the Oscar-nominated production powerhouse for Muse, their first full album together after 20 years of friendship. Primarily written and recorded at Williams’ Louis Vuitton HQ studio in Paris, the two superstars spend the 16-track set blending luscious string arrangements with hard-hitting horns and 808s for what Legend calls a “Black James Bond aesthetic.” — K.D.
